item.title: Rtd Major Gen Golam Mohiuddin arrested over New Gini Properties attack
item.description:
Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested Major (retd) General Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury over the attack at New Gini Properties in the capital’s ECB Chattar area.
Golam Mohiuddin was an “ezhar listed” accused in the case, said deputy commissioner (media) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police Akhtar Hossain.
However, DB did not disclose when or from where the person was arrested.
Earlier, police arrested Shahrier, the suspected mastermind as of the attack and vandalism, at content creator Salman Muqtadir’s Brownfish Studio and the surrounding land at ECB Chattar in the capital.
Cantonment Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Gias Uddin said the attack stemmed from a dispute between New Gini Properties Limited, owner of the land where the studio is located, and other landowners in the area.
Police said Salman Muqtadir had set up the studio by renting a floor from New Gini Properties.
The studio was vandalized during the attack, police said.
Salman alleged that a group of people arrived in two trucks and attacked the studio late Saturday night.
In a live broadcast from the Brownfish Studio Facebook page, Salman said the studio was completely destroyed.
He later alleged that the attackers’ main target might have been the owner of the property, who apparently refused to pay extortion money.
OC Gias Uddin said New Gini Properties, which was in possession of the land and rented out the studio space to Muqtadir, had erected a gate on the land, restricting access for others.

item.title: Mariyam's family reaches settlement in case against MP Nazrul
item.description:
A settlement has been reached with the family of victim a case filed over the alleged abetment of suicide of Gazi Nazrul Islam’s second wife, Mariyam Akter.
The matter was disclosed during a bail hearing before Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah on Wednesday.
The complainant, Mariyam's father Masum Billah, said he had no objection if Gazi Nazrul and his first wife, Maksuda Islam, were granted bail.
Earlier, on September 20, police recovered the hanging body of Mariyam, 19, from Flat 203 of NAM Bhaban in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar. The door was locked from inside.
With assistance from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), police broke open the door and recovered her body hanging from a ceiling fan. Several notes were also found in the room.
The following day, Masum Billah filed a case against Nazrul Islam, his first wife Maksuda Islam and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman, accusing them of abetting her suicide.
Police arrested Nazrul and Maksuda that night.

item.title: Home minister: Crackdown on extortionists, criminals to be intensified
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Wednesday drives against terrorists, armed criminals, drug dealers and extortionists are underway and would be intensified further.
“Lists of terrorists, armed criminals, drug dealers and extortionists are always maintained by the police and regularly updated,” he said responding to a question from reporters after a meeting at the Secretariat on preparations for Durga Puja celebrations.
The police department is regularly collecting data on the number of terrorists, drug dealers and extortionists arrested, and the information is being published in the media, he added.
The home minister said the country’s overall law and order situation should not be assessed based on one or two isolated incidents, stressing that the government is continuing its efforts to ensure public safety and maintain peace in society.
“We have always told you this. We speak to the press almost every day. We are continuing our efforts to ensure the security of people and establish peace in society,” he said.
Asked about allegations of land grabbing and extortion using political influence, Salahuddin said the government considers a criminal a criminal irrespective of political identity.
He said police respond immediately to calls made to the national emergency service 999, go to the spot, make arrests and file cases.
“Whoever is involved, strict action will be taken against them and is being taken,” he said.
Asked about the role of a former lawmaker in an incident in Mirpur, the Home Minister said the matter is under investigation.
Regarding the incident at Radda Clinic, he said negligence of duty has been found on the part of a police officer. “The officer was immediately withdrawn and departmental action has been initiated against him.”
The minister also said there was no political involvement in the Radda MCH-FP center incident.
However, he said some of those involved in crimes might have political identities, but the government was taking legal action against them without considering their political affiliations.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,108 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,108.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,007, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 101, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The four new suspected fatalities were reported across four divisions; Dhaka, Sylhet, Chittagong, and Mymensingh with one death each.
A total of 1,221 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 191,731.
During the same period, 128 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 21,520.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 169,800 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 162,873 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Home minister: Coordination gap during eviction drive might be behind Mirpur clash
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Wednesday said a lack of coordination among the authorities responsible for the hawker eviction drive could be behind clashes at Mirpur in the capital when a police vehicle and three city corporation vehicles were set on fire.
He made the remarks while responding to questions from reporters after a meeting at the Secretariat on preparations for celebrating Durga Puja.
Asked whether there was prior intelligence about the city corporation’s plan to conduct the eviction drive with police support, the home minister said he had ordered an investigation into the incident.
“From what I have learned initially, I have ordered an investigation. I learned that the magistrate responsible and the officials from the city corporation or RAJUK did not properly communicate with the police. I think there was a lack of coordination,” he said.
He added that the matter would be investigated further.
A clash broke out between hawkers, Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) officials and police during an eviction drive at Mirpur in the capital on Wednesday.
The eviction drive began around 10am from Mirpur-10 to Mirpur-14 as part of the DNCC’s efforts to clear footpaths and roads of illegal encroachments.
At one stage, the hawkers clashed with city corporation officials and law enforcement personnel.
A city corporation vehicle was set on fire and a police vehicle was vandalized during the clash, said witnesses.
Several media workers were also attacked allegedly by the hawkers while covering the incident.

item.title: BFIU seeks bank account details of Salman Muqtadir
item.description:
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) has sought details of bank accounts held in the name of content creator Salman Muqtadir.
A letter was sent to banks and financial institutions across the country on Wednesday, with officials from several banks confirming receipt of the letter.
The BFIU has requested account opening forms, Know Your Customer (KYC) documents, transaction records and other relevant information related to accounts held in Salman’s name. Banks have been instructed to provide the information within a specified timeframe.
It was not immediately clear why the BFIU sought the information.
The request comes amid ongoing discussions surrounding an attack, vandalism and looting at Salman Muqtadir’s Brownfish Studio at New Guinea Properties in the capital’s ECB Chattar area.
The studio was attacked on Saturday night, causing extensive damage. The New Guinea Properties office and several nearby structures were also reportedly vandalized.
Saiful Islam Bhuiyan, a director of New Guinea Properties, filed a case with Cantonment police station over the incident, accusing the attackers of trespassing, vandalism, looting and theft. Police and the Detective Branch (DB) have arrested several people in connection with the case.
Following the attack, Salman Muqtadir initially alleged that it was related to extortion.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed later said a preliminary investigation indicated that the incident stemmed from a dispute over around 35 kathas of land.
According to the home minister, the dispute involved New Guinea Properties and a party linked to a retired military officer. Salman’s studio, located on the premises, was also targeted during the attack.
The home minister also said spent bullet casings and locally made weapons were recovered from the scene.
Police have also linked the attack to the land dispute, saying a group of people attacked the property following a conflict over its entrance and access routes. Some of those arrested have also been accused of being involved in planning the attack.
Following the home minister’s remarks, Salman said he had gone to Cantonment police station on the night of the incident to file a case.
He alleged that police were initially reluctant to register the case, although it was eventually accepted. His statements on the matter have been reported by several media outlets.
On September 29, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Broadcasting Zahed Ur Rahman also mentioned Salman by name, saying content creators with large audiences should exercise greater responsibility in their future conduct.
Against the backdrop of the attack, the land dispute and the subsequent statements, the BFIU’s request for information on Salman’s bank accounts has drawn attention.
Sources said banks will now provide the requested account, transaction and related financial information to the BFIU as instructed.

item.title: Clash during Mirpur footpath eviction drive, vehicle set on fire
item.description:
Clashes, vandalism and arson broke out in the capital’s Mirpur-10 area on Wednesday afternoon during a drive to clear footpaths of encroachment.
A vehicle of Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) was reportedly set on fire, while a police vehicle and an excavator used in the drive were also vandalized.
Md Shahidul Islam, duty officer at Mirpur Model Police Station, confirmed the incident and said law enforcement personnel were working to bring the situation under control.
Police said hawkers had long occupied footpaths in the Mirpur-10 area, operating temporary shops and businesses.
The city corporation launched the drive to remove the encroachments. At the start of the operation, an argument broke out between hawkers and city corporation workers, eventually leading to clashes and counter-chases.
Vandalism and arson were reported at several locations during the unrest.
Witnesses said a city corporation vehicle was set on fire during the clash. A police vehicle and an excavator used in the eviction drive were also reportedly vandalized.
Initial information suggested that a fire first broke out at one location due to an electrical short circuit while the drive was under way. Later, some agitated hawkers allegedly set fire to a city corporation garbage truck.
Two Fire Service units responded to the incident and brought the blaze under control.
Additional police were deployed in the area following the incident, with law enforcement personnel remaining on alert to maintain public safety and traffic movement.
The drive was part of the city corporation’s regular efforts to clear footpaths of encroachment, officials said.
Police said those involved in the incident would be investigated and necessary action taken.

item.title: Malaysia's ex-PM Mahathir in hospital for observation
item.description:
Malaysia's 101-year-old former prime minister Mahathir Mohamad has been hospitalised for observation, his aide told AFP, following the death on Monday of his wife of seven decades.
The two-time prime minister was admitted to the National Heart Institute in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday night, aide Sufi Yusoff said, though the reason for his hospitalisation was not immediately known pending an official diagnosis.
Sufi said Mahathir had not been getting enough rest following the passing of his wife, Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, on Monday and was feeling fatigued.
"He is in a stable condition," Sufi told AFP in a WhatsApp message on Wednesday.
"He is exhausted from the emotional ups and downs, the hot weather and lack of rest. All of that is not a good combination for someone who is 101 years old," he added.
His wife Siti Hasmah, who was a medical doctor and an advocate for public health, passed away at the age of 100. The couple raised seven children together.
Mahathir, visibly grief-stricken by her death, told the country's former king through tears that he "didn't expect her to die today", in footage recorded at her funeral and posted on his official Instagram account.
Mahathir has suffered several heart problems in recent years and underwent bypass surgeries.
The centenarian has been hospitalised repeatedly in recent years, and most recently in January after suffering a hip fracture in a fall.
He has been dubbed the world's oldest-serving leader after helming office twice, first holding the position as the Southeast Asian country's fourth national leader from 1981 until 2003.
He then served as prime minister for a second time at the age of 92 from 2018 to 2020.

item.title: Gold prices rise
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has raised gold prices in the domestic market, with the price of 22-carat hallmarked gold increasing by Tk190 per gram.
Under the new rates, 22-carat hallmarked gold is priced at Tk19,785 per gram, up from Tk19,595 on Tuesday.
Bajus said the new rates were set after considering the overall market situation, particularly the rise in the price of pure gold (tejabi gold).
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Wednesday and will remain in effect at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring at 9am on September 30.
Under the new rates, 21-carat gold is priced at Tk18,895 per gram, while 18-carat gold is priced at Tk16,225 per gram. Gold made using the traditional method is priced at Tk13,255 per gram.
The price of one bhori (11.664 grams) of 22-carat gold now stands at approximately Tk230,781. Making charges will be added separately, depending on the design of the jewellery.
The price of 22-carat gold was Tk19,595 per gram on September 29, meaning the price per bhori has increased by approximately Tk2,214.
Bajus had reduced gold prices several times before the latest increase. On September 28, 22-carat gold was priced at Tk19,785 per gram, while the price stood at Tk19,970 per gram on September 26.
Bajus has also increased silver prices.
The price of 22-carat silver has been set at Tk370 per gram, while 21-carat silver is priced at Tk355, 18-carat silver at Tk305 and traditional-method silver at Tk230 per gram.
The price of 22-carat silver was Tk355 per gram on September 29, representing an increase of Tk15 per gram.
According to a Bajus notification, VAT is included in the fixed selling price and cannot be collected separately from customers.
Making charges, however, will apply separately depending on the design of the jewellery.
For the exchange of old gold jewellery, a 12% deduction applies, excluding making charges and stone costs. An 18% deduction applies when purchasing old gold jewellery.
Bajus said VAT cannot be deducted separately in cases of exchange or purchase.
The fixed prices will remain effective at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.

item.title: HC questions why three women were stopped from travelling abroad
item.description:
The High Court on Tuesday issued a rule questioning the legality of preventing three adult women from travelling to Nepal despite having valid passports, entry permits and flight tickets.
The court also directed the concerned additional inspector general of police to investigate the complaints about the incident at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on August 8 and take necessary measures within seven days. It ordered the police to submit a compliance report.
The court further directed immigration authorities not to obstruct the three women from travelling abroad in future without a lawful basis.
The bench of Justice KM Kamrul Kader and Justice Fatema Anwar passed the order after hearing a writ petition filed by Rifa Tamanna, Sohani Islam Somapty and Najnin.
The three women, who are involved with the Bangladesh International Mediation Society (BIMS), were travelling to Nepal on August 8 as mediators to attend a conference, said their lawyer Ishrat Hasan.
She said Nepal provides visas on arrival to Bangladeshi citizens and that travellers from Bangladesh only need an Electronic Travel Authorization.
According to the petition, immigration officials stopped the women despite having the required documents, allegedly because they were unmarried and travelling without their parents or guardians.
In the rule, the court asked why the authorities’ actions should not be declared illegal.
It also asked why guidelines should not be formulated to ensure that adult women are not prevented from travelling abroad lawfully because they are unmarried, travelling without their parents or guardians, or on similar gender-based grounds.
The secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs, the inspector general of police, an additional inspector general of police, Police Headquarters and the immigration officials concerned have been made respondents to the rule.
Advocate Ishrat Hasan appeared for the petitioners, assisted by lawyer Tanzila Rahman Jui. Additional Attorney General Mohammad Arshadur Rouf opposed the writ petition.

item.title: A child’s innocence and a world of cruelty
item.description:
There are images that travel through social media because they are extraordinary. Then there are images that travel because they reveal something painfully ordinary about us.
The video from Uzirpur, Barishal, belongs to the second category. A little girl sits beside her father, who is tied to a roadside pole after being accused of theft. She dips pieces of bread into tea and feeds him with her own hands. Around them, people watch. Someone records. Later, thousands of people watch the recording.
The image is heartbreaking, but perhaps we should resist the temptation to stop at heartbreak.
The child has become the emotional centre of the story, but the real question is not simply why she fed her father. The more uncomfortable question is why her father was left tied to a pole in the first place.
According to reports, the man was detained by local people in Bamrail Bazar, Uzirpur, late on September 25 over an alleged attempt to steal. He was reportedly beaten and tied to a pole overnight. Police were informed but arrived after he had already been released by locals. No formal complaint was filed at the time.
Later, the upazila administration became involved, and officials arranged for the man to be taken to a rehabilitation centre following allegations of drug use. The administration also said it would support the child's education and help her mother find employment. The theft allegation itself remains a matter of conflicting accounts and has not been established through a judicial process.
That distinction matters. A person may be guilty of theft. He may have a history of offending. He may struggle with addiction. None of these possibilities gives a crowd the authority to become judge, jury, and jailer.
This is where the incident becomes larger than one accused man in one market. It forces us to ask what happens when the machinery of justice is replaced by the impatience of the crowd.
We often speak about the rule of law as though it were an abstract constitutional principle. In reality, the rule of law begins with something much more basic: A person accused of a crime remains a person.
The French novelist Victor Hugo understood this moral complication remarkably well. In Les Misérables , Jean Valjean's theft of bread is not presented simply as a question of whether stealing is right or wrong. Hugo asks us to look at the social world that surrounds the act.
The crime matters, but so does the hunger, exclusion, and desperation that make the crime intelligible. Understanding an offense does not mean excusing it. It means refusing to reduce a human being to the worst thing he may have done.
That distinction seems particularly relevant here. If the allegations against the man are true, he should face the consequences established by law. If he is struggling with addiction, he needs treatment. If poverty or family circumstances contributed to his situation, society should address those conditions.
None of these responses requires compassion to replace accountability. Rather, genuine accountability requires a system capable of distinguishing punishment from humiliation.
What happened in Uzirpur appears to have done the opposite. Before the facts were established, punishment came first. The rope came before the verdict.
There is another unsettling element in the video. The crowd did not merely restrain a man. His humiliation became public theatre. People gathered around him. Some reportedly demanded harsher treatment. A passerby recorded the scene and uploaded it to Facebook.
The video then travelled far beyond the market. The same technology that allowed the public to witness the injustice also transformed a child's distress into a piece of viral content.
This is one of the darker contradictions of the social media age. We are increasingly able to see suffering, but seeing suffering does not necessarily make us more humane. Sometimes it simply makes us spectators.
Hannah Arendt's writings on the relationship between ordinary people and systems of wrongdoing offer a useful philosophical lens here. Great harm does not always require extraordinary villains. Sometimes it emerges through ordinary people surrendering moral responsibility to the crowd, the institution or the situation.
The frightening question is not whether every person present intended cruelty but whether anyone stopped to ask the simplest question: What gives us the right to do this?
And then came the child.
She did not investigate the theft allegation. She did not ask whether her father was innocent. She did not know the procedural language of justice. She simply saw a hungry and humiliated human being whom she knew as her father. Her response was not a legal argument. It was an act of recognition.
Perhaps that is why the image unsettled so many people. The adults around the pole were looking at an accused thief. The child was looking at her father.
There is something profoundly important in that difference.
Modern societies build institutions precisely because human emotions are unreliable. Anger demands immediate punishment. Fear demands protection. Revenge demands spectacle.
Law is supposed to slow these impulses down. It asks us to investigate, establish facts, hear both sides, and impose proportionate consequences. In that sense, due process is not a luxury for respectable people. It is a protection for everyone, including those we dislike.
Immanuel Kant argued that human beings should never be treated merely as means to an end. The principle is particularly powerful here. A person accused of theft cannot become an object through which a crowd demonstrates its anger or moral superiority. Nor should a child's emotional suffering become entertainment for thousands of viewers.
The most encouraging part of this story came after the video spread. The administration intervened, arranged rehabilitation for the father, and promised support for the child's education and her mother's livelihood.
These steps are important because they recognize that punishment alone cannot solve problems involving addiction, poverty, and family vulnerability.
But institutional intervention should not depend on virality.
That may be the most important lesson from the incident. What if nobody had recorded the video? What if the child had not been there? What if the image had not touched the emotions of millions? Would the man still have been released? Would anyone have asked about his family? Would anyone have considered the child's education?
A society in which compassion arrives only after a video goes viral is a society that has outsourced conscience to the algorithm.
We should also be careful about romanticizing the father-daughter scene. It is tempting to say that the video proves that the man is a good father despite everything else. We do not know enough to make such a conclusion.
A single tender moment cannot erase allegations or family difficulties. Nor should the child's love be used to excuse any wrongdoing. Children can love people whose actions are deeply flawed. That is precisely what makes childhood both beautiful and vulnerable.
The little girl did not prove her father's innocence. She revealed our responsibility. Her small hands holding bread may have done something that the adults around the pole failed to do. They restored his humanity.
Perhaps that is why we should remember the image differently. Not as a sentimental story about a loving daughter, and not as evidence that an accused man was either good or bad. We should remember it as a question placed before an entire community.
When someone is accused of a crime, do we want justice, or do we simply want someone to suffer?
The difference between those two desires is the difference between a society governed by law and one governed by the crowd.
And sometimes, astonishingly, it takes a child with a piece of bread dipped in tea to remind the adults of that difference.
HM Nazmul Alam is an academic, journalist, and political analyst based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Currently he teaches at IUBAT. He can be reached at nazmulalam.rijohn@gmail.com .

item.title: Zero tolerance for organized land grabs
item.description:
The alarming wave of violence pertaining to land grabs sweeping across Dhaka over recent days marks a dangerous collapse of civil order that must be met with uncompromising force from our authorities concerned.
That within three days, four separate properties across the capital -- Radda clinic in Mirpur, a housing compound in Mohammadpur, a residential building in Adabor, and a creative studio at ECB Chattar -- were targeted by organized, armed mobs shows just how dire the state of law and order is currently in the country.
How is it that hundreds of hired goons, wielding guns, machetes, and heavy machinery, can arrive in trucks to intimidate residents, vandalize structures, and seize land? This is no longer merely a series of civil property disputes but brazen gang violence, and it must end immediately.
Whatever political realignments have taken place since August 2024, the fundamental premise of a law-governed society remains unchanged: Legal ownership and possession must be determined exclusively through the judiciary and not through mob mobilization. This should not be a complex matter to grasp.
We must once again question our law enforcement agencies and their utter failure in preventing attacks of such massive scale. While recent arrests and stern promises from top police officials are at least a step in the right direction, words alone will not reassure a terrified citizenry.
We need the state to institute an absolute, zero-tolerance policy against organized land grabbing. Law enforcement must hunt down, arrest, and prosecute not only the hired foot soldiers, but crucially the ones calling the shots and orchestrating these operations.
There is simply no room for error on the part of our law enforcement, who must become more effective, not just at apprehending these criminals but also gathering intelligence to prevent such attacks.
If the state fails to crush this emerging apparatus of mob intimidation with unyielding resolve, it surrenders the capital to anarchy, and undermines any development ambitions we have. We cannot allow that to happen.

item.title: Daraz Bangladesh extends support to flood-affected families beyond immediate relief
item.description:
Bangladesh has always lived with water. The monsoon feeds its fields and shapes its villages, and every so often floodwaters leave homes, possessions and livelihoods damaged in their wake. Emergency relief may address the immediate need, but for affected families, recovery continues long after the water recedes.
Over 12 years in Bangladesh, Daraz has built a nationwide ecosystem connecting customers, sellers and communities across the country. That presence has also shaped how the company approaches support for communities affected by natural disasters, extending its role beyond immediate emergency assistance.
This approach informed Daraz's response to this year's monsoon floods in Moulvibazar in Sylhet and in Satkania and Banshkhali in Chattogram.
The company committed approximately $30,000, around Tk36 lakh, to a multi-phase program covering three areas, essential relief for more than 900 families, targeted rehabilitation support for households identified as requiring further assistance, and flood-safety awareness for a further 1,000 families.
The relief packages, containing dry food, hygiene essentials and first-aid items, were the first step.
The program then moved into a more targeted rehabilitation phase. Alongside the distribution, Daraz volunteers spoke with affected families to assess the extent of damage and identify households requiring additional support. Those households received assistance based on their individual needs, including roofing sheets and bamboo for repairing damaged shelters, bedding and mosquito nets, cooking stoves and utensils, and safe-drinking-water supplies.
Kamrul Hasan, chief commercial officer of Daraz Bangladesh, said: "Daraz is part of many families' everyday lives, and when those families face a disaster, standing beside them is our responsibility. Relief is where we begin, and helping people rebuild is what we are committed to."
The people doing the work were Daraz's own. 20 colleagues from 5 department volunteered, sorting supplies, travelling to the affected areas and listening to families. "Our colleagues are members of these communities too," said Syed Abdullah Morshed, Chief People Officer of Daraz Bangladesh. "Participation was voluntary, and colleagues chose to give their time to support affected families directly. Their involvement reflects the sense of responsibility our people feel towards the communities in which we operate."
On the ground, project coordinator Sayem Hossain led the assessment work. "In Satkania and Banshkhali, we walked through neighbourhoods where the water had gone but its marks were everywhere, mud lines high on the walls, tin roofs and bamboo fences bent or washed away, bedding and cooking pots lost," he said. "The families were not asking for much. They wanted a livable place to sleep, a roof they could trust and something to cook on. We sat in courtyards and asked each family what they had lost. Some homes needed a new roof, others needed only bedding. Deciding who needed help most was hard, because everyone had lost something."
This is not Daraz's first response to a natural disaster. In 2024, the company reached more than 85,000 flood-affected people across multiple districts. While that response focused on providing immediate assistance at scale, this year's program introduces a more targeted rehabilitation component.
For Daraz Bangladesh, the program reflects a broader shift from responding only to the immediate consequences of a disaster to supporting recovery and preparedness as well.
For the families in Moulvibazar, Satkania and Banshkhali, that means support extending beyond the distribution of emergency supplies to rebuilding homes, restoring basic household needs and helping communities prepare for future flooding.

item.title: Honor introduces its connected ecosystem vision at Honor Connect
item.description:
Honor Bangladesh showcased its latest developments in AI and connected technology at Honor Connect on September 29. Held at the United Convention Center in Dhaka, the event highlighted the company’s expansion beyond smartphones into a broader connected ecosystem.
The Robot Phone made its local introduction at the event, alongside the unveiling of its new brand logo.
The program centered on Honor’s new “Dare to Be” philosophy, which reflects the brand’s approach of making technology more adaptive to people’s needs and more closely integrated into everyday life.
The company also announced Magic9 Pro's local arrival in the coming months.
Launched globally on September 28, the flagship is built in collaboration with ARRI, the cinema camera maker.
Filmmaker Raihan Rafi and cinematographer Sumon Sarker, who have worked on several prominent Bangladeshi film projects, attended as special guests and led a session on ARRI technology.
Speaking at the event, Honor SEA Region’s GTM Director Leo Pei said: “honor may have started as a smartphone brand here, but a phone is now only part of what we build. Our phones, tablets, wearables, laptops and TVs are designed to work together and adapt to how people use them.”
“People in Bangladesh want technology that fits naturally into their everyday lives, not technology that they have to work around. The Robot Phone is only one example of what the full Honor ecosystem can do, and there’s so much more to unfold,” said Lang Guo, country manager, Honor Bangladesh.
Mohammad Zahirul Islam, managing director of Smart Technologies (BD) Limited, said: “As you know, Honor is currently doing local manufacturing in Bangladesh, and our local manufacturing performance is on par with the best factories in the world. We will gradually bring Honor’s gadgets to the Bangladeshi market.”
“We have been serving customers through our partners since 1998 and have delivered millions of devices to customers so far,” he added. “We remain open to customers' advice and criticism, and we make necessary changes accordingly.”
Holding Honor’s Robot Phone, filmmaker Raihan Rafi said: “I felt that I could make an experimental short film with this. Our cameras are often very large, which limits the kind of shots we can get. This creates challenges in situations like shooting inside a car, among many others. One advantage I see in this camera is that we can place it anywhere and shoot. The camera movement is also very interesting. If someone is running, the cinematographer does not have to run with the camera. The camera can automatically capture it.”
Abdullah Al Mamun, head of business, and Syed Md Badrul Arifeen, director and head of product and marketing, also spoke at the event.
The event also featured an experience zone, where guests explored the brand's ecosystem products.
Alongside the Robot Phone, the lineup included Magic V6, Honor's latest foldable.
Other smartphones, tablets, earbuds, headphones and smartwatches were on display as well.
Guests also got an early look at the company's upcoming laptops and TVs, ahead of their arrival in Bangladesh.
These products are set to mark Honor's large-scale entry into both categories in the country, with a multi-series laptop lineup and TVs spanning 32 to 100 inches with the latest display technologies.

item.title: Health minister: Lifestyle changes needed to prevent heart disease
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has called for healthier lifestyle choices and greater public awareness as non-communicable diseases continue to rise in Bangladesh.
He made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at a public seminar titled “Every Heartbeat is Life” at the National Heart Foundation in Mirpur, Dhaka, on Wednesday, marking World Heart Day.
The program was chaired by National Heart Foundation President Prof Dr Khondker Abdul Awal Rizvi.
The health minister said the government has taken several initiatives to bring healthcare services closer to people.
Work is underway to increase the capacity of all upazila health complexes from 50 to 151 beds, he said.
The government also plans to establish 10 dialysis centers at district-level hospitals and 50 at medical college hospitals, according to the minister.
These initiatives will help reduce pressure on hospitals in Dhaka and allow people in different parts of the country to receive necessary treatment closer to home, he said.
Sakhawat said the government had allocated the highest-ever budget for the health sector this year, stressing that improving healthcare infrastructure alone would not be enough without adequate manpower.
A nationwide recruitment process for nurses has already begun, while police verification of selected candidates is underway, he added.
The minister also expressed concern over rising HIV infections in the country.
He stressed the need to strengthen preventive measures and raise public awareness to address the growing burden of non-communicable diseases.
Textile and Jute Ministry Secretary Sharaf Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, National Heart Foundation Secretary General Prof Fazila-Tun-Nesa Malik, Directorate General of Medical Education Director General Prof Nazmul Hossain and Prof Sohel Reza, among others, attended the program.

item.title: Nagoya mayor says sorry for Asian Games 'inconveniences'
item.description:
Nagoya's mayor apologised to athletes on Wednesday for "inconveniences" at the Asian Games in the Japanese city following a string of complaints.
The continent's biggest sporting event has been dogged by problems including a shortage of beds and issues with transport.
There are over 17,000 athletes and officials, more than the Olympics, and countries have accused local organisers of mismanagement.
"We must offer our apologies to the athletes and others affected by these inconveniences," said Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa, who is also acting chairman of the local organising committee.
"We must sincerely reflect on the mishandling that occurred," he added.
"There were human errors and a lack of communication with the national teams.
"We are responding based on what has happened."
Unlike past Games, there is no athletes' village in a bid to save money, with participants instead sleeping in temporary wooden units, on a cruise ship and in hotels.
Some teams have complained about the temporary cabins, even saying the beds are too short.
Early in the Games local organisers apologised to South Korea after the North Korean national anthem was played by mistake.
There have been issues with buses for athletes not running when they should, not turning up at all or going to the wrong venues.
Some athletes were also stranded for hours at the airport when they landed in Nagoya for the start of the Games on September 19.
The Games, which are taking place in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture, end on Sunday.

item.title: Brazil football clubs face massive sponsorship blow from betting ban
item.description:
Brazil's powerhouse football clubs are reeling after a ban on sports betting companies, their biggest sponsors, which has left multi-million dollar deals in limbo.
Flush with cash from their betting sponsors, Brazilian clubs have in recent years dominated their South American rivals, winning the last seven Copa Libertadores titles.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who on Sunday is facing a tight election race against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro on Friday signed a provisional measure banning online betting companies, dubbing the industry a "cancer."
This is what is at stake:
- How much do clubs rake in? -
Fourteen of the 20 clubs in Brazil's top-flight Brasileirao have a betting company as their main sponsor.
That money accounted for 34 percent of clubs' commercial revenue in 2025, or around $200 million, according to investment firm Galapagos Capital.
Flamengo, the reigning Libertadores and Brasileirao champion, has the biggest annual sponsorship deal in South American football history with Betano, worth $46 million.
That is equivalent to what the team paid this year for midfielder Lucas Paqueta, setting a new benchmark in the South American market.
"How am I going to pay for Paqueta?" Flamengo president Luiz Eduardo Baptista said on a podcast following the ban.
The measure "puts future revenue, the contracts we have signed and the payments we have to make at risk," he said.
- What happens now? -
Lula's measure orders betting adverts to be removed after October 5.
A meeting between the government and clubs this week was postponed until after Sunday's first-round election, a Sports Ministry source told AFP.
The Senate has 120 days to decide whether to turn the provisional measure into law.
The main betting industry associations on Monday asked the Supreme Court to suspend the measure, alleging that it is unconstitutional.
Lula has doubled down saying either he "puts an end to betting, or betting will put an end to Brazil."
The president argues that betting companies account for "just" seven percent of clubs' revenues.
- What are the risks for clubs? -
Experts warn that clubs face a possible devaluation of their commercial assets and potential legal action.
"An indebted company, a company without legal certainty that cannot honor its commitments, suffers a devaluation," said Fabiana Bentes of sports industry institute Sou do Esporte.
The loss is "very large," said Cruzeiro owner Pedro Lourenco.
"We are looking at the situation and reviewing the accounts. It is not easy to quantify the scale of the loss today," he added.
The Belo Horizonte club will nevertheless receive financial support from the Minas Gerais state government, which announced assistance for local clubs that have lost their sponsors.
Fluminense president Mattheus Montenegro said it will not be easy for clubs to replace these sponsors.
"It is obvious that this devalues the asset, because any company interested in sponsoring a football club will have almost all the clubs available at the same time," he told CNN Brasil.
- How will this impact Brazil's regional dominance? -
Flamengo said in a statement that revenue from online betting has "propelled Brazilian football to the point of dominating" South American competitions.
Betting sponsorships of Brazilian clubs emerged in 2019, filling a space left by state-owned bank Caixa Economica Federal.
Since then, 12 of the 14 Libertadores finalists have been Brazilian teams.
According to specialist website Transfermarkt, nine of the 10 most valuable clubs in the region are in the Brasileirao.

item.title: Coaches selected for six D3 Trophy teams
item.description:
The six teams in Bangladesh’s new D3 Trophy selected their coaching staff through a management draft in Dhaka on Tuesday, two days after the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) formally announced the tournament.
Sohel Islam was picked as head coach of Ace Bluestar, Rajin Saleh by Acme, Mizanur Rahman by Citizens Bank, Mohammad Salahuddin by Fortune Group, Talha Zubair by Seven Rings Cement and Abdur Razzak by Walton Group.
The draft was held at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium, where the BCB presented the teams with a list of 35 coaches from which they selected their staff.
Each team picked a head coach, two assistant coaches, a physiotherapist, a strength and conditioning coach and an analyst.
The D3 Trophy, formally called the Domestic Three Trophy, is part of a restructuring of Bangladesh’s domestic cricket calendar. The BCB will combine the three formats under one tournament, with the T20 competition beginning on December 15, followed by the four-day competition in January and the one-day competition in May.
The BCB has awarded six institutions the rights to operate the six teams for three years at a cost of taka 250 million each per year.
National team batting coach Mohammad Ashraful and bowling coach Talha Zubair are also among the coaches selected for the tournament.
They will work with their D3 teams when the national team have no commitments.
Teams can also appoint coaches who went unselected in the draft if a member of their coaching staff is unavailable.
The assistant coaches selected were Humayun Kabir and Hannan Sarkar by Seven Rings Cement; Faisal Hossain and Tarek Aziz by Acme; Dollar Mahmud and Tushar Imran by Walton; Abdul Qayyum and Mohammad Ashraful by Fortune Group; Mohammad Selim and Najmul Hossain by Citizens Bank; and Ashikur Rahman and Salauddin Ahmed by Ace Bluestar.

item.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of 'misinformation' campaign in bid for World Cup papers
item.description:
FIFA has accused European football's governing body UEFA of a "misinformation" campaign in its bid to access documents related to Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off parts of the World Cup.
In FIFA's response in a court case in Florida, it says UEFA's attempt to force the world body to hand over the documents is also an attempt to "influence" next year's FIFA presidential election.
FIFA president Infantino caused uproar in July with proposals to create a commercial subsidiary to run its biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.
The plan would have allowed private investors to acquire stakes in a company created under the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative. The backlash that followed led to the proposals being quickly shelved.
FIFA says in its court filing that UEFA makes "numerous false or misleading statements" about Infantino and the world governing body, including that "Infantino sought to profit personally from the FFE proposal".
AFP has contacted UEFA for its response.
UEFA, home to World Cup holders Spain and football powerhouses such as France, England and Germany, is leading the opposition to Infantino, calling openly for his removal.
FIFA confirmed this month that Infantino will stand again for president in the election next March, despite the backlash over his now-abandoned private investment plan.
Infantino sent a letter to FIFA's 211 members this week indicating that a greater amount of money could be distributed to FIFA members from its cash reserves.
In the letter seen by AFP, Infantino said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered".
Infantino insisted in the letter that the abandoned proposal to sell off World Cup commercial rights had been intended to generate additional money for football.
"The recent commercial proposal, now withdrawn, was intended to enable FIFA to invest more in football," Infantino wrote.
Infantino is not without friends -- 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with African football's governing body CAF and South America's CONMEBOL also supportive.

item.title: Albert becomes youngest US scorer in 4-2 win over Chile
item.description:
Mathis Albert became the youngest-ever US goal-scorer and fellow teen Julian Hall netted in back-to-back games as Mauricio Pochettino's side beat Chile 4-2 in a friendly international Tuesday at St Louis.
Hall created Sebastian Berhalter's opener with a clever dummy, then became the youngest US player to score in his first two appearances before defensive stalwart Chris Richards slammed in a header.
Albert, 17 years and four months old, slammed in a fourth in stoppage time, surpassing Christian Pulisic to become the team's youngest-ever goalscorer.
Diego Ulloa and Maximiliano Gutierrez had briefly put Chile ahead with goals either side of half-time.
A night that began with an emotional pre-game send-off ceremony to World Cup captain Tim Ream, who confirmed his international retirement, proved to be another full of promise for Pochettino's reinvigorated roster.
Fresh from thumping Peru 4-1 at the weekend, when 11 players had made their debuts, Pochettino sent out the youngest line-up yet of his two-year tenure, with an average age of 23 years and 25 days.
Gio Reyna was the only player retained from Saturday's win, with Antonee Robinson captaining for the first time.
After scoring on debut, Hall squandered the first decent chance of the game. Played through one-on-one by Berhalter, the 18-year old rounded Chile's goalkeeper, but blasted his shot wastefully over.
Chile grew dangerous on the break. England-born Chile winger Ben Brereton Diaz lashed the crossbar with a fizzing effort, and Dario Osorio rattled the left post with a curling shot.
But the US struck on their own counter-attack. Sergino Dest rolled a sideways pass across penalty spot. Hall made a brilliant dummy, letting it through his feet to Berhalter, who slammed into the bottom-left corner.
In first-half stoppage time, Chile equalized. Another dangerous Osorio corner was parried twice by Brady, his second punch sending the ball back goalward. An almighty goalmouth scramble followed before Ulloa bundled it in.
The game had barely resumed when Chile struck again. Gutierrez won an aerial duel on the halfway line, sprinted toward goal, cut inside, and curled a beautiful finish into the bottom corner.
But barely two minutes later, Hall got his goal, leaping to steer a glancing header from Reyna's lifted cross into the net for 2-2.
Pochettino rang five changes soon after the hour mark, bringing on several more experienced players from the recent World Cup campaign.
Among them was Richards, who quickly slammed home a powerful header from Berhalter's pinpoint outswinging corner.
Deep in stoppage time, Albert's shot rocketed into the crossbar and down across the line -- a goal that was confirmed by the referee moments later, and surpassed Pulisic's 2016 goal against Bolivia in the team history books.
Tempers boiled over as both squads and coaching staff flooded onto the pitch for a bout of shoving and shouting before and the final whistle.

item.title: Yamal brace inspires Spain to Croatia romp, England down Czechs
item.description:
Lamine Yamal netted a brace as world champions Spain continued their winning start to the UEFA Nations League with a 4-1 success in Seville against Croatia on Tuesday, while Harry Kane scored as England won in the Czech Republic.
The match at the Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan was Spain's first home outing since lifting the World Cup in New York in July.
La Roja captain Rodri was handed the trophy by 2010 winner and Sevilla legend Jesus Navas, before presenting it to the ecstatic crowd.
"We were very excited to bring the trophy here," Yamal said.
"To be able to win the game and bring it home is great."
Spain's supporters did not have long to wait before their side provided further excitement in Andalusia as Yamal fired them into the lead inside 75 seconds.
Dion Beljo nodded in Ivan Perisic's cross to briefly level the scores shortly before the half-hour, but Atletico defender Marc Pubill popped up at the other end three minutes later to head in a Yamal centre and restore the hosts' lead.
After also scoring early in Spain's 3-2 win at Wembley against England last week to kickstart their Nations League campaign, Yamal brought his tally in the 2026/27 edition of the tournament to three as he put Spain two clear of Croatia in the 63rd minute with a precise finish at Dominik Livakovic's near post.
"Lamine is keen to keep developing and show the world the sort of footballer he is," Luis de la Fuente said of the 19-year-old star.
"We've enjoyed his magic in the service of the team. In the future, he'll be much more recognised for what he does and for his contribution to the team's play," the coach added of Yamal, who is among the frontrunners for the Ballon d'Or.
Nico Williams then put gloss on the result for Spain with a crisp step-over and finish with one minute remaining on the clock.
With two wins from two, Spain lead Group A3 on six points, while Croatia sit third on three points, behind second-placed England on goal difference.
In Prague, Thomas Tuchel's England got their first win of the group with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Czech Republic thanks to second-half goals from Anthony Gordon and Kane.
The home team kept England at bay in the first half at the Fortuna Arena despite being a man down after Pavel Sulc was sent off for a high challenge on Elliot Anderson in the 23rd minute.
"We played very professional, second half we stepped up... Deserved victory," Tuchel told ITV.
"Strange to get an early red card, not the best for the team and spectators. It's an awkward one but we kept going, got a win and that's what counts."
Barcelona winger Gordon broke the deadlock shortly after the break with a header from a cross served by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who made his first England start in almost two years.
It was Gordon's third goal in three games for England, including one against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final defeat and another against Spain.
Kane, who also scored against Spain, gave England breathing space in the 69th minute, smashing the ball past Czech 'keeper Matej Kovar after it fell to him inside the box.
England will travel to Rijeka to take on Croatia on Saturday, while Spain welcome the Czechs to Oviedo.
"The next match is important for us against a direct opponent and we want to win," Tuchel said to the BBC.
Elsewhere, Scotland paid for an early red card at Hampden Park against Switzerland as the visitors ran out 3-0 winners in Group B1.
Slovenia sit second in that pool after downing North Macedonia 2-0 in Ljubljana.

item.title: Salman Muqtadir's studio attack was staged, claims Mir Shahe Alam
item.description:
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam has alleged that the attack on content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio was staged and that the blame was subsequently shifted to the BNP.
“The perpetrators themselves orchestrated the attack on Salman Muqtadir’s studio, yet the blame was shifted onto the BNP. Ironically, the person arrested in connection with the incident is the son-in-law of a Jamaat MP. Such incidents clearly reveal the underlying conspiracy,” he said.
He made the remarks around 8pm on Tuesday while addressing a rally following a torchlight procession organised by the Shibganj upazila and municipal BNP units.
The program was organised to protest what BNP leaders described as conspiracies, orchestrated terrorism and anarchy by clandestine and banned groups.
The state minister alleged that clandestine and banned groups were engaging in subversive activities as part of a plot to bring former prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to the country.
“Through various conspiracies, they are attempting to destabilise the nation and mislead the public. However, they must bear one thing in mind: the people of this country will no longer accept Sheikh Hasina,” he said.
He said the government was working to meet people’s expectations, maintain democratic continuity and uphold law and order.
“No form of terrorism, anarchy or conspiracy aimed at disrupting this progress will be tolerated,” he said.
Mir Shahe Alam also said the BNP had come to power through street-level movements and struggles with public support.
“Therefore, threatening the BNP with ouster is futile; the party cannot be suppressed through conspiracies or intimidation,” he said.
Earlier, Mir Shahe Alam led the torchlight procession, which began at the Shibganj Upazila Parishad premises.
A large number of BNP leaders and activists from its affiliated organisations took part in the procession before joining the rally organised by the Shibganj upazila and municipal BNP units.

item.title: Sagar-Runi murder case report deferred for 130th time
item.description:
A Dhaka court has deferred the submission of the investigation report in the murder case of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi to November 5, marking the 130th time the report has been deferred.
Wednesday was the scheduled date for submitting the report. However, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), which is investigating the case, failed to submit it.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam then set November 5 as the new date for submission.
Sub-Inspector Rafiqul Islam of the prosecution division confirmed the matter.
The accused in the case are Rafiqul Islam, Bakul Mia, Masum Mintu, Kamrul Islam alias Arun, Abu Sayeed, security guards Palash Rudra Pal and Enayet Ahmed, and the couple’s friend Tanvir Rahman Khan.
Tanvir is currently out on bail, while Palash went into hiding after securing bail. The other accused remain in custody.
Sagar Sarowar, news editor at Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were murdered at their residence on February 11, 2012. Following the incident, Runi’s brother, Nausher Alam Roman, filed a murder case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.
Initially, a sub-inspector of the police station was assigned to investigate the case. Four days later, the investigation was transferred to the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.
After more than two months, the DB failed to resolve the case, and the High Court subsequently handed the investigation over to the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) on April 18, 2012.
On September 30 last year, the High Court ordered the formation of a high-powered task force comprising experienced investigators from various agencies to investigate the murders. The court also directed that the investigation be completed within six months and ordered RAB to be removed from the investigation.
Following another High Court directive, the Public Security Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs issued a notification on October 17 last year forming the task force.
A four-member task force was subsequently formed, with the PBI chief serving as its convener.

item.title: "A vibrant democracy requires a vibrant media"
item.description:
The media has a vital role in promoting youth’s active participation in policymaking and institutional reform. In light of the significant role played by them in the July 2024 mass uprising, speakers at a roundtable today, Wednesday, emphasised the need to ensure their meaningful involvement in decision-making processes.

They also discussed how the media can amplify their concerns and perspectives and strengthen public discourse on good governance, accountability, and democratic development.

With a shared commitment to strengthening the role of media in democratic reform and decision-making, the roundtable discussion was held in Dhaka today. The discussion aimed to highlight youth’s priorities, concerns, and recommendations while exploring the role of media in democratic participation, accountability, institutional reform, and the protection of civic rights.

The event was organised by VOICE and The Bangladesh Dialogue (TBD) under the Joining Youth in Effective Engagement in Reform Agendas in Bangladesh (JoYEE) project.

Speaking at the discussion, Kamal Ahmed, Consulting Editor of The Daily Star, said, “A vibrant democracy requires a vibrant media. Therefore, youth need to continue demanding reforms and calling for accountability and responsibility from both media organisations and political actors.”

Senior journalist and columnist Sohrab Hassan said, “The media needs to play a more active role in bringing the younger generation’s expectations and concerns into broader public discussions rather than limiting them to dialogue alone. Greater cooperation and engagement between youth and media can help ensure that their expectations are effectively reflected in policymaking and implementation.”

Ayesha Kabir, Head of Content, English Web, Prothom Alo, said, “Media serves as a vital bridge in bringing the youth voices into public discourse and the mainstream of democratic reform. It is important to present their perspectives objectively and based on evidence, while also providing in-depth analysis of issues that matter to the new generation.”

In his concluding remarks, Ahmed Swapan Mahmud, Executive Director of VOICE, said, “Participation of the youth must not be limited to consultation or symbolic representation. Institutional mechanisms are needed to enable them to influence decision-making, ensure institutional accountability, and play a meaningful role in the reform process.”

The discussion was attended by youth representatives and editors, sub-editors from various media organisations. Speakers emphasised the importance of combining the experience of older generations with the energy of younger ones to advance the country. They also highlighted the need to increase the representation of women and indigenous journalists in media leadership positions.

The discussion concluded with a call to strengthen accountability in reform implementation and enhance the role of media in ensuring meaningful youth participation in democratic and institutional reform processes of Bangladesh.

item.title: West Indies pile up record 405-7 in second ODI against India
item.description:
CRICKET-IND-WIS-ODI

Opener John Campbell hit 101 to lay the foundations for West Indies' highest-ever one-day international total of 405-7 against India in their second match on Wednesday.

Skipper Shai Hope (104) and Amir Jangoo (114) also struck centuries to boost the total as West Indies look to bounce back in the three-match series, led by India 1-0, in Guwahati.

Invited to bat first, West Indies lost Keacy Carter for nine before Campbell and Hope put on 110 runs to set the tone for the batting domination.

West Indies' previous ODI best was 389 against England in 2019, but they ended up losing the match.

Campbell reached his second ODI hundred but in the next over fell to pace bowler Gurnoor Brar after the opener hit nine fours and five sixes in 68-ball knock.

Hope and left-handed Jangoo put on 182 runs for the third wicket as the pair hammered the opposition attack with regular boundaries on a batting-friendly pitch.

Hope, a wicketkeeper-batter, raised his 20th ODI ton to go past West Indies legend Brian Lara's 19 hundreds.

Chris Gayle has the most ODI centuries for West Indies with 25 tons.
Jangoo reached his second ODI hundred off 70 balls, leaping up and punching the air in delight.

West Indies lost three quick wickets including Hope, Sherfane Rutherford -- out for a first-ball duck -- and then Jangoo, dismissed by Ravindra Jadeja.

Left-arm wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav struck twice to reach 200 ODI wickets before Roston Chase with his unbeaten 29 took West Indies past 400.

India will need a record chase, one surpassing their ODI best of 362 against Australia in Jaipur in 2013.

item.title: Exam papers stolen from trunks, photocopied in office chamber, smuggled in underwear
item.description:
“That SIM has run out of balance. Dad, send a message; I’m waking everyone up. Have you taken money from anyone?” Comes the reply from the other end: “It’s raining; I’ll speak once I’m free. How many have you taken so far?” The response comes: “50 people will be cleared now.”

This exchange took place between Syed Abed Ali, a former driver for the Bangladesh Public Service Commission (BPSC), and his son, Syed Sohanur Rahman Siam.

In another text message sent by a member of this syndicate, it reads: “Ibrahim Bhai, the work on the 5th is 100 per cent confirmed. Not a single point will stray. Trusting in Allah, I give you my word—I will deliver every single task 100/100 to you. All money must be cleared by the 21st. Send a PDF of each application one day before formal submission. Once we check and give clearance, you may submit.”

In another message to a candidate, it is said, “It is essential to complete this job, brother. We must help this candidate succeed in the viva on the 3rd.”

Instructions follow from the other side: “Tomorrow, please make time to pay the money for the Land Records candidate. And leave the money for the Sub-Assistant Engineer’s viva before you go.” To clear the written examination, the demand is made: “Bhai, if you want to pass the written exam, it will cost Tk 700,000.”

Regarding the railway recruitment examination papers, another message reads: “Money is required upfront—Tk 100,000. Must be paid now. The results will be published within two to three days.” The person on the other end says: “Do not say anything until I give clearance... How is the other group? What is the status of the group of 12?”

Numerous WhatsApp messages recovered by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) reveal an extensive network involved in question paper leaks and job-peddling across various government recruitment examinations, including the BCS (Bangladesh Civil Service) and BPSC (Bangladesh Public Service Commission) non-cadre tests.

Although driver Syed Abed Ali was the public face of the operation, the masterminds of these dealings were some officials and employees inside the PSC, alongside a syndicate within the Government Printing Press (BG Press).

According to court sources, following a lengthy investigation, investigating officer and CID Additional Superintendent of Police Suman Kumar Saha submitted a charge sheet against 55 individuals on 18 May. Among them, 37 face a separate money laundering probe.

Of the 55 accused, 26 were arrested; one remains in prison, while 25 others—including Abed Ali and Siam—are currently out on bail. Twenty-nine suspects remain at large.

Owing to lack of evidence, the CID recommended discharging Md. Zakaria Rahman, an officer of the 31st BCS Police Cadre, from the case. However, although Md. Golam Hamidur Rahman, Hamidul Islam Zia, Md. Mahabub Alam, and Azad were involved in the incident, the investigative agency has yet to verify their full names and addresses.

On 9 July 2024, CID Sub-Inspector Nippon Chandra Chanda filed the case at Paltan Police Station. On 15 September, the court instructed that the names of the absconding accused be published in newspapers via public notice by 25 October.

Photocopied inside the officer's chamber

The most shocking details regarding the theft of question papers emerged around BPSC Office Assistant Md. Sajedul Islam (Accused No. 4 in the case). In January 2024, Sajedul devised the primary scheme to steal question papers for the recruitment examination of Sub-Assistant Engineers for Bangladesh Railway, conducted by the BPSC.

According to investigative case files, Sajedul took advantage of the absence of BPSC officer Golam Faruq prior to the examination. Obtaining the key from BPSC cleaner Rupan Chandra Das, he entered Golam Faruq's chamber. Using a hacksaw blade he had brought along, he cut open the lock of a trunk to extract four sets of handwritten question papers meant for final moderation. Unwilling to risk taking them outside, he photocopied all four sets on the official photocopying machine inside the chamber itself. He then placed the original question papers back into the trunk exactly as they were and relocked it, ensuring no external suspicion was raised.

To prevent the leaked papers from originating from a single source, Sajedul had the questions typed up piecemeal at various computer shops across Dhaka, including Dainik Bangla Road and Shantinagar. Two days before the railway recruitment examination, Sajedul met Abed Ali in front of the Ramna Park gate and handed over the four sets of questions (comprising 800 multiple-choice questions in total). In return, Sajedul personally received Tk 7.5 million.

Sajedul’s involvement extended beyond the railways recruitment tests; he played an active role in leaking the preliminary question papers for the 46th BCS examination as well. Sajedul and Khalilur Rahman supplied 17 candidates to Abu Solaiman Md. Sohel, 13 of whom passed. Sajedul pocketed Tk 1.6 million from this transaction alone.

Furthermore, a major portion of the approximately Tk 8 million collected from 40 candidates for the Polytechnic Junior Instructor recruitment exam went straight into Sajedul’s pockets.

The CID has uncovered vast assets registered under his name and pseudonyms across various parts of the country. In a statement given under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Sajedul confessed to all his crimes before the court.

Question papers smuggled in underwear

Outside the BPSC, the primary source of leaked question papers was the BG Press. Investigations revealed that binding worker Mohammad Akram Hossain and cleaner Majnu Miah bypassed strict security measures to smuggle out the papers.

Akram had long-standing ties with ATM Golam Mostafa, a compositor at BG Press and a fugitive accused in the case. In 2012, Akram sold the preliminary examination papers for the BCS to Mostafa for Tk 260,000. The investigation detailed how Akram extracted the printed papers: while packaging the questions, he would discreetly slip into the washingroom to photograph them on his mobile phone. On other occasions, he would tuck complete question papers inside his underwear to carry them outside.

Cleaner Majnu Miah similarly smuggled question papers out by hiding them in his underwear. All sets of question papers for the Railway Sub-Assistant Engineer examination were brought outside of the BG Press through Akram and Majnu, before being supplied to ATM Golam Mostafa and Mizanur Rahman for vast sums of money.

According to the CID, this constituted the most secret and secure layer of the leak ring.

Suspended, reinstated, and back to leaking

Md. Khalilur Rahman, accused No. 3 in the case, had worked as a dispatch writer at the BPSC since 2005. In 2012, he was caught red-handed and dismissed from service for leaking written examination papers for the 33rd BCS. However, he was reinstated to his BPSC post in 2022. Upon his return, Khalilur engaged in leaking question papers on an even larger scale. Assisted by his neighbour Bipash Chakma, he procured question papers to sell to job applicants.

Investigative findings show that for the railway recruitment exams, Khalilur took Tk 120,000 from Niamul Hasan, Tk 800,000 from Anisur Rahman, Tk 400,000 from Mahbubur Alam, and Tk 400,000 from MM Najmul Hasan. Out of the funds collected from various individuals, he handed over Tk 3.5 million to Sajedul Islam. On the day preceding the railway exam alone, Khalilur presented 98 examinees directly to Sajedul.

Upon Khalilur’s arrest, the CID seized mobile phones, exam admit cards, multiple-choice question sets, cheques, stamp papers, as well as a secret diary and notebook. The diary contained meticulous financial accounts listing job seekers’ names, mobile numbers, transaction amounts, and registration numbers.

Rise under the "elder brother"

Atikul Islam became involved in leaking question papers in 2001. After a relative of his became a member, Atikul began visiting the BPSC regularly and discovered the BG Press-based syndicate.

Atikul and BG Press worker Golam Mostafa were arrested while renting a resort named 'Bhinno Jogot' in Rangpur to leak question papers for the secondary school assistant teacher recruitment examination in 2010.

When Atikul was jailed, his driver Md. Mizanur Rahman and Mizanur’s brother-in-law Md. Al Mamun ran the network in his stead, later aligning themselves with Syed Abed Ali’s group.

Brought into the illicit business by Atikul was his younger brother, Md. Mojahedul Islam, 36. Prior to the 35th BCS examination, Mojahedul and his friends memorised four sets of leaked questions—totaling around 800 questions—at a residence in Manipuri Para, Dhaka. The exact same questions appeared in the exam.

Later, in 2018, Mojahedul obtained the complete question sets for the administrative officer recruitment examination under the Department of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) from his elder brother Atikul prior to the test. Taking the exam with those leaked papers, he successfully secured the position of Administrative Officer.

Once employed as a government official, Mojahedul became a full-fledged “question paper merchant” himself. For the Railway Sub-Assistant Engineer exam alone, he collected nearly Tk 10 million from candidates, depositing Tk 3 million into the Dutch-Bangla Bank account of Abed Ali’s firm, 'Rashida Traders'.

Earlier in 2023, he collected Tk 600,000 per person from 29 candidates and Tk 900,000 per individual from 14 candidates for the positions of Instructor and Junior Instructor under the Technical Education Board.

For the 45th BCS, he kept three candidates at a guesthouse in Kalyanpur to have them memorise the question papers. He subsequently invested his illicit earnings into various domestic and overseas businesses.

The garment factory owner

Md. Noman Siddique discovered the syndicate in 2015 while searching for medical exam question papers for his wife. He has been acquainted with Khalilur Rahman since 2014. Obtaining the medical question papers and selling them to Khalilur marked his debut in this underworld.

Later, he established an exclusive monopoly over collecting and selling question papers for recruitment exams across various sectors—including Assistant Revenue Officer, ATEO, Senior Staff Nurse, Assistant Personal Officer, the Ministry of Defence, and the Teacher Registration examinations.

The CID discovered approximately Tk 120 million in 14 bank accounts held under Noman's personal and corporate names. Using the proceeds from question paper leaks, he established a garment factory named 'Ittehad Fashion & Apparels' in Ashulia.

Abed Ali's Tk 410 million empire

The ultimate coordinator of this entire network was former BPSC driver Syed Abed Ali Jibon. Having joined the BPSC in 1997, he drove official cars for then-chairmen Mujibur Rahman Biswas and Mozammel Huq.

Exploiting internal vulnerabilities, he initially built a network of proxy examinees. By placing two fake candidates on either side of an actual candidate during examinations, the proxies would dictate the answers to the main applicant. Earning between Tk 100,000 to 150,000 per job, he accumulated an initial Tk 2.5 million.

Between 2000 and 2005, he solidified his position by securing government jobs for individuals in exchange for payments. After leaving his job in 2013, he teamed up with Khalilur through Mahfuz Kalu in 2015.

Under the guise of securing jobs as Revenue Officers at the NBR, he transacted Tk 3.2 million with Atikul and Tk 3.6 million with Kalu. The CID traced Tk 412.9 million across 12 bank accounts owned by Abed Ali and his business entities. For the Railway Sub-Assistant Engineer exam, he fielded 44 candidates, collecting nearly Tk 40 million in advance.

item.title: Fuel prices unchanged for October
item.description:
The government has decided to keep fuel prices unchanged for October, with diesel, kerosene, petrol and octane retaining their current retail prices.
From Thursday, October 1 diesel will sell at Tk135 per litre, kerosene at Tk155, petrol at Tk160 and octane at Tk165.
